craft_evidence.owned: Claimed with partial evidence: brand's own blog (29 Jan 2020) places "the El Paso factory" at its Walter Jones Blvd location, with a factory worker of 33 years and 150-200 steps per boot; Our Process page photographs hand-stitching, lasting and hand-tooling (no facility named there); El Paso shirt copy says El Paso is "where Lucchese's renowned bootmaking factory resides"; Fox Business 25 Oct 2025 cites "the company's manufacturing facility in El Paso". No filing found; owned vs leased not established. Apparel is not made there.
craft_evidence.makers: NONE (0 of 139 apparel pages name a maker; boots say "Handmade in Texas" without naming the plant)
craft_evidence.mills: NONE (generic only: "Italian denim" on Dean jeans, Peruvian/Supima/Pima cotton, "Fabric made in Italy" on one sport coat)
craft_evidence.madein: apparel 34 of 139 styles (24%): Italy 18, USA 7, Vietnam 6, India 2, Canada 1; boots/shoes 194 of 278 men's feed records (70%): "Handmade in Texas" 183, Italy 11
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed: 1883, San Antonio (shop near Fort Sam Houston), Sicilian brothers Salvatore and Joseph Lucchese; incorporated 1929; moved to El Paso 1986 (brand timeline; Texas HR 2374, 2023)
craft_evidence.process: yes for boots (brass and lemonwood pegging, hand-lasted instep, hand stitching, hand tooling, matched crocodile skins, stonewashing; twisted-cone last on the timeline); no for apparel
craft_evidence.reasoning: Boots, the core of the house, are made by Lucchese itself in El Paso: the brand's own blog names the factory's Walter Jones Blvd location and a 33-year worker, the Our Process page documents pegging, hand lasting and tooling, and 70% of men's boot/shoe records say "Handmade in Texas". The facility is named by street only (no filing, ownership unproven), and the apparel range is sourced (Italy, Vietnam, India, USA, Canada) with no named makers or mills, so 4 rather than 5.

ownership.owner: Lucchese, Inc., private; chairman John Muse says "I bought Lucchese and sold off the other attached brands" after it became available in 1997 (brand blog, 5 Aug 2020); no current filing read

opview: “I tell my family that we are caretakers of this brand.” — John Muse, chairman and owner, Lucchese, The Last Word blog, "52 Faces of Lucchese: John Muse"
